summary: Hrishikesh Terdalkar works in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed a BSc at Chennai Mathematical Institute and a PhD at IIT Kanpur under Arnab Bhattacharya, Pralay Manna, and Sowmya Krishnapur, later holding posts at IIT Kanpur, Lyon 1, BITS Pilani, and IIIT Hyderabad.

Specializing in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Hsiang-Kuang Chou studied under Swami Shivananda. His career included serving as Professor of Chinese at the University of Allahabad, Lecturer at the University of Delhi and LBSNAA, and Chancellor of Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy.

Hsiao-Lan Hu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Hu completed a PhD at Temple University and served as an associate professor of Religious Studies & Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy.

Hsing Yun (1927–2023) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. He studied under teachers including Zhikai and Yinshun, trained at institutes like Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy, founded Fo Guang Shan, and served as its abbot from circa 1967 to 1985.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Hsu Yun (1840–1959) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. In 1953, he founded the Buddhist Association of China and served as its honorary president.

Hsu-feng Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Lee completed a master's degree at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and earned a PhD from the University of Sydney under Mark Allon.
Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist studies teacher who studied under Chang Zhi and Hsu Yun. He founded the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, serving as its abbot from circa 1976 to 1995.
Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held academic posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo from circa 1976 to 2014.

Hu Shih (1891–1962) was a philosopher and Sinologist. He studied at Cornell and Columbia under John Dewey and Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

Huabei Tan specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Tan pursued an English-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Medawachchiye Dhammajothi.

Huai-Chin Nan (1918–2012) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who studied under Huanxian Yuan. He taught at Chinese Culture University, National Chengchi University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and the Republic of China Military Academy.

Huaiyu Chen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser, later becoming an assistant professor at Arizona State University circa 2008.

Huaiyuan Yu specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Yu completed a Bachelor of Laws at Xiamen University, earned an MSc at University College London, and became a PhD candidate at Xiamen University in 2023.

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, having studied at UCLA. He has held appointments at Zhejiang University, the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Sun Yat-sen University, the University of Macau, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Huawen Bai (1930–2021) was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Bai studied at Peking University from circa 1951 to 1955 and subsequently served there as a professor from circa 1955 to 2000.

Hubert Decleer (1940–2021) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under Étienne Lamotte at KU Leuven. He served as academic director and senior faculty advisor at SIT Graduate Institute, and held visiting roles at Middlebury College and the University of Vienna.

Hubert Durt (1936–2018) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held long-term posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, the Hōbōgirin Institute, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and became an associate professor at Ohio State University circa 1998.
Hugh Canning (d. 1927) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned an MA at Trinity College, Hartford, by 1910 and became its Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology in 1914.
